card.name: Possessive words before owned things
card.fires_on: Possessive words such as their, his, her, its, my, our, or family/families, placed before something a person or group owns or belongs to (work, brand, territory, citizens, businesses).

modes.label: Possessive pronouns
modes.description: A possessive pronoun like their, his, her, its or our follows a verb or preposition and refers back to a subject.
modes.example: Seeing the pride the kids had for<< their>> work proved how valuable the project was,

modes.label: Family as possessor
modes.description: The word family or families is used as a possessive-like modifier before a noun.
modes.example: Copies of important<< family>> documents, such as insurance policies, identification

card.writes: It seems to favor an owned noun next and to suppress words like own and neighbor, which are possessive-adjacent.
card.plain: It fires on words like "their" or "his" that point to whose thing is about to be named.
